literal: The prince again recorded Masters of Writing affairs; newly appointed officials had to visit the prince to thank him for their posts, and on leaving had to take leave.
idiomatic: Prince of Changshan again recorded Masters of Writing affairs; newly appointed officials had to visit him to thank him for their posts, and on leaving had to take leave.

literal: Xi said to the prince: "To receive rank from the heavenly court and pay thanks at a private residence has from antiquity been held a breach of protocol.
idiomatic: Wang Xi said to the prince, "To receive rank from the heavenly court and pay thanks at a private residence has from antiquity been held a breach of protocol.

literal: Civil and military officials of the court, coming and going with thanks and farewells — it should all be stopped at once.
idiomatic: Civil and military officials of the court, coming and going with thanks and farewells — it should all be stopped at once.

literal: The sovereign is attentive; he relies on Your Highness to support him.
idiomatic: The sovereign is attentive; he relies on Your Highness to support him.

literal: " The prince accepted this.
idiomatic: " The prince accepted this.

literal: He often said calmly to Xi: "The sovereign's conduct is unsteady; you see and hear what he does — can I really stay silent forever because I once provoked his anger?
idiomatic: He often said calmly to Wang Xi, "The sovereign's conduct is unsteady; you see and hear what he does — can I really stay silent forever because I once provoked his anger?

literal: You should draft a memorial of remonstrance; I will seize a suitable moment and remonstrate to the utmost.
idiomatic: You should draft a memorial of remonstrance; I will seize a suitable moment and remonstrate to the utmost.

literal: " Xi then set out more than ten items and presented them.
idiomatic: " Wang Xi then set out more than ten items and presented them.

literal: He remonstrated sharply with the prince: "The court is now like this — do you wish to follow some reckless commoner who treats a morning's life lightly? Madness-drug makes a man unaware of himself; blade and arrow no longer know kin from stranger. If disaster suddenly comes from beyond reason, what of Your Highness's household estate — what of the empress dowager!
idiomatic: He remonstrated sharply with the prince, "The court is now like this — do you wish to follow some reckless commoner who treats a morning's life lightly? Madness-drug makes a man unaware of himself; blade and arrow no longer know kin from stranger. If disaster suddenly comes from beyond reason, what of Your Highness's household estate — what of the empress dowager!

literal: I beg you for now to yield and go along, and be more careful day by day.
idiomatic: I beg you for now to yield and go along, and be more careful day by day.

literal: " The prince sobbed uncontrollably and said: "Has it come to this?
idiomatic: " The prince sobbed uncontrollably and said, "Has it come to this?

literal: " Next day he saw Xi and said: "I thought all night; now my mind is at rest.
idiomatic: " Next day he saw Wang Xi and said, "I thought all night; now my mind is at rest.

literal: " He ordered fire and burned the draft before Xi.
idiomatic: " He ordered fire and burned the draft before Wang Xi.

literal: Later the prince seized an opening and remonstrated bitterly, until he offended the sovereign's will.
idiomatic: Later the prince seized an opening and remonstrated bitterly, until he offended the sovereign's will.

literal: The emperor had brawny men twist his arms behind him, drew a bare blade and set it to his neck, and cursed: "What does a stripling know — you mean to deny me with clerkly talent; who taught you?
idiomatic: Gao Yang had brawny men twist his arms behind him, drew a bare blade and set it to his neck, and cursed, "What does a stripling know — you mean to deny me with clerkly talent; who taught you?

literal: " The prince said: "The realm holds its tongue; apart from your servant, who dares speak?
idiomatic: " The prince said, "The realm holds its tongue; apart from your servant, who dares speak?

literal: " The emperor urged them on to beat him; they flogged him with clubs dozens of times; he happened to be drunk and asleep and was spared.
idiomatic: " Gao Yang urged them on to beat him; they flogged him with clubs dozens of times; he happened to be drunk and asleep and was spared.

literal: Thereafter his lewd pursuits spread among kin; wherever he went he lingered, turning day into night — only at the Changshan residence he often found no fit occasion and left.
idiomatic: Thereafter Gao Yang's lewd pursuits spread among kin; wherever he went he lingered, turning day into night — only at the Changshan residence he often found no fit occasion and left.

literal: When the emperor died, Jinan succeeded to the throne.
idiomatic: When Gao Yang died, Prince of Jinan succeeded to the throne.

literal: The prince said to Xi: "One man holds court at ease; we too shall keep our ease.
idiomatic: The prince said to Wang Xi, "One man holds court at ease; we too shall keep our ease.

literal: " He added that the court was lenient, benevolent, and forgiving — a true heir who guarded the patrimony, a good ruler.
idiomatic: " He added that the court was lenient, benevolent, and forgiving — a true heir who guarded the patrimony, a good ruler.

literal: Xi said: "In the Tianbao era fortunes held; the eastern palace was entrusted to a barbarian. Now he suddenly oversees all affairs, driving fierce men.
idiomatic: Wang Xi said, "In the Tianbao era fortunes held; the eastern palace was entrusted to a barbarian. Now he suddenly oversees all affairs, driving fierce men.

literal: If His Sagehood is young and not equal to many trials, yet others hand in and out the imperial edicts, power is sure to settle somewhere.
idiomatic: If His Sagehood is young and not equal to many trials, yet others hand in and out the imperial edicts, power is sure to settle somewhere.

literal: Though Your Highness wish to keep to princely duty, can you?
idiomatic: Though Your Highness wish to keep to princely duty, can you?

literal: If far-off orders let you retire in modesty, do you yourself judge that the house and throne can endure long?
idiomatic: If far-off orders let you retire in modesty, do you yourself judge that the house and throne can endure long?

literal: " The prince fell silent in thought; after a long while said: "How am I to be placed?
idiomatic: " The prince fell silent in thought; after a long while said, "How am I to be placed?

literal: " Xi said: "The Duke of Zhou held King Cheng in his arms and received the feudal lords, regent seven years, then returned the government and made the son clear sovereign — fortunately there is precedent; only Your Highness must weigh it.
idiomatic: " Wang Xi said, "The Duke of Zhou held King Cheng in his arms and received the feudal lords, regent seven years, then returned the government and made the son clear sovereign — fortunately there is precedent; only Your Highness must weigh it.

literal: " The prince said: "How dare I liken myself to the Duke of Zhou.
idiomatic: " The prince said, "How dare I liken myself to the Duke of Zhou.

literal: " Xi said: "Your Highness's standing today — can you avoid the Duke of Zhou?
idiomatic: " Wang Xi said, "Your Highness's standing today — can you avoid the Duke of Zhou?

literal: " The prince did not answer.
idiomatic: " The prince did not answer.

literal: When the emperor set out, he ordered the prince to follow the carriage; Xi was made chief administrator of Bing.
idiomatic: When the emperor set out, he ordered the prince to follow the carriage; Wang Xi was made chief administrator of Bing.

literal: When the prince reached Ye, Yang, Yan and others were executed; an edict made the prince grand chancellor, commander-in-chief of all armies within and without, overseeing civil and military affairs; he returned to Bing.
idiomatic: When the prince reached Ye, Yang Yin, Murong Yan and others were executed; an edict made him grand chancellor, commander-in-chief of all armies within and without, overseeing civil and military affairs; he returned to Bing.

literal: He then summoned Xi and said: "Because I did not heed your words early, petty men wielded power and I nearly came to ruin.
idiomatic: He then summoned Wang Xi and said, "Because I did not heed your words early, petty men wielded power and I nearly came to ruin.

literal: Though by the ruler's side it is briefly cleared, in the end how am I to be placed?
idiomatic: Though by the ruler's side it is briefly cleared, in the end how am I to be placed?

literal: " Xi said: "Your Highness's former standing could still be weighed by name and teaching in going forth and withdrawing.
idiomatic: " Wang Xi said, "Your Highness's former standing could still be weighed by name and teaching in going forth and withdrawing.

literal: Today's situation turns on heaven's timing; it is no longer within human reason.
idiomatic: Today's situation turns on heaven's timing; it is no longer within human reason.

literal: " Before long it was memorialized that Prince of Zhao Commandery Rui be left chief administrator, and Xi be chief marshal.
idiomatic: " Before long it was memorialized that Prince of Zhao Commandery Gao Rui be left chief administrator, and Wang Xi be chief marshal.

literal: Each night he was brought in by carriage; by day they did not speak — because Xi was scholarly and slow, fearing he would not suit the generals' mind.
idiomatic: Each night he was brought in by carriage; by day they did not speak — because Wang Xi was scholarly and slow, fearing he would not suit the generals' mind.

literal: Later the prince entered a private room and said: "Of late the princes and great men each press me, saying I go against heaven and invite ill fortune — fearing some change may rise. I mean to hold them by law.
idiomatic: Later the prince entered a private room and said, "Of late the princes and great men each press me, saying I go against heaven and invite ill fortune — fearing some change may rise. I mean to hold them by law.

literal: " Xi said: "The court of late has kept kin at distance — does it consider the weight of bone and blood?
idiomatic: " Wang Xi said, "The court of late has kept kin at distance — does it consider the weight of bone and blood?

literal: Your Highness's hasty acts are no longer the matter of a minister; a thorn in the back, crossed halberds at the neck — above and below doubting each other; how can it last?
idiomatic: Your Highness's hasty acts are no longer the matter of a minister; a thorn in the back, crossed halberds at the neck — above and below doubting each other; how can it last?

literal: Moreover heaven's way is not constant; loss and gain pile on; spirit and omen shift — subtle signs gather.
idiomatic: Moreover heaven's way is not constant; loss and gain pile on; spirit and omen shift — subtle signs gather.

literal: Though you hold modesty and restraint, to treat the sacred vessel like chaff is to go against the Supreme One's intent and wreck the late emperor's foundation.
idiomatic: Though you hold modesty and restraint, to treat the sacred vessel like chaff is to go against heaven's intent and wreck the late emperor's foundation.

literal: " The prince said: "How dare you speak what should not be spoken — I must bring you to law.
idiomatic: " The prince said, "How dare you speak what should not be spoken — I must bring you to law.

literal: " Xi said: "I hold that heaven's timing and human affairs share one measure; therefore I offend the thunder, fearless of axe and halberd.
idiomatic: " Wang Xi said, "I hold that heaven's timing and human affairs share one measure; therefore I offend the thunder, fearless of axe and halberd.

literal: Today I may lay bare heart and liver — perhaps the spirits also approve.
idiomatic: Today I may lay bare heart and liver — perhaps the spirits also approve.

literal: " The prince said: "To rescue difficulty and set up support waits for a sage; how dare I debate in private — please speak no more.
idiomatic: " The prince said, "To rescue difficulty and set up support waits for a sage; how dare I debate in private — please speak no more.

literal: " Soon an edict said the chancellor's burden was heavy and all staff advanced one grade; Xi as chief marshal also held the post of gentleman in the ministry of personnel.
idiomatic: " Soon an edict said the chancellor's burden was heavy and all staff advanced one grade; Wang Xi as chief marshal also held the post of gentleman in the ministry of personnel.

literal: Chancellor attendant Lu Yao was about to go on mission; on parting he clasped Xi's hand and said: "The great prince's merit fills the realm, the realm joyfully urges him on, songs fill the roads, things have no different wish.
idiomatic: Chancellor attendant Lu Yao was about to go on mission; on parting he clasped Wang Xi's hand and said, "The great prince's merit fills the realm, the realm joyfully urges him on, songs fill the roads, things have no different wish.

literal: We wish to bare our loyal hearts, but suddenly receive outer mission, with no face-to-face way to speak our brief loyalty — our inch of heart we respectfully raise to you.
idiomatic: We wish to bare our loyal hearts, but suddenly receive outer mission, with no face-to-face way to speak our brief loyalty — our inch of heart we respectfully raise to you.

literal: " Xi soon repeated Yao's words.
idiomatic: " Wang Xi soon repeated Yao's words.

literal: The prince said: "If inside and outside alike have different hopes, Zhao Yanshen is morning and evening at my side — why has he never spoken of it?
idiomatic: The prince said, "If inside and outside alike have different hopes, Zhao Yanshen is morning and evening at my side — why has he never spoken of it?

literal: Try my meaning and speak of it secretly to him.
idiomatic: Try my meaning and speak of it secretly to him.

literal: " Xi seized a moment and asked Yanshen; Yanshen said: "I too of late was startled by these songs; each time I wished to report, my mouth locked and my heart trembled.
idiomatic: " Wang Xi seized a moment and asked Yanshen; Yanshen said, "I too of late was startled by these songs; each time I wished to report, my mouth locked and my heart trembled.

literal: Younger brother has now begun the theme; I too will risk death and bare heart and liver once.
idiomatic: Younger brother has now begun the theme; I too will risk death and bare heart and liver once.

literal: " He then likewise urged him on.
idiomatic: " He then likewise urged him on.

literal: At that time the princes and generals and the four quarters' governors memorialized the mandate's signs.
idiomatic: At that time the princes and generals and the four quarters' governors memorialized the mandate's signs.

literal: In the eighth month of the first year of Ganming, Emperor Xiaozhao ascended the throne.
idiomatic: In the eighth month of the first year of Ganming, Emperor Xiaozhao ascended the throne.

literal: In the ninth month Xi was made attendant cavalier; he still held concurrently gentleman in the ministry of personnel.
idiomatic: In the ninth month Wang Xi was made attendant cavalier; he still held concurrently gentleman in the ministry of personnel.

literal: Later, when a memorial audience ended, the emperor said calmly: "Of late why do you act like an outsider guest — you are hardly to be seen at all.
idiomatic: Later, when a memorial audience ended, the emperor said calmly, "Of late why do you act like an outsider guest — you are hardly to be seen at all.

literal: From now, unless it is office business, whenever you have something in mind, make a slip as fits and when a brief opening appears bring it straight in.
idiomatic: From now, unless it is office business, whenever you have something in mind, make a slip as fits and when a brief opening appears bring it straight in.

literal: " He ordered Director of the Masters of Writing Yang Xiuzhi, Director of Ceremonies Cui Jie, and one other — three men — each day when their proper duties ended, all to enter the eastern corridor and together record rites fallen and music lost through the ages, offices abolished, court sacrifice differences, carriage dress additions and subtractions.
idiomatic: " He ordered director of the Masters of Writing Yang Xiuzhi, director of ceremonies Cui Jie, and one other — three men — each day when their proper duties ended, all to enter the eastern corridor and together record rites fallen and music lost through the ages, offices abolished, court sacrifice differences, carriage dress additions and subtractions.

literal: Or men of lofty virtue long sunk in obscurity;
idiomatic: Or men of lofty virtue long sunk in obscurity;

literal: or clever words dazzling the vulgar and evil spirits harming government — reaching taxes on fields, markets, boats and carts, levies open or blocked, marriage and burial rules, noble and base full mourning — whatever was inconvenient in the time yet used unceasingly from old and new, or useful in antiquity yet destroyed today: all were to think in detail, report item by item in time, not wait until all was ready; when memory returned, continue the report.
idiomatic: or clever words dazzling the vulgar and evil spirits harming government — reaching taxes on fields, markets, boats and carts, levies open or blocked, marriage and burial rules, noble and base full mourning — whatever was inconvenient in the time yet used unceasingly from old and new, or useful in antiquity yet destroyed today: all were to think in detail, report item by item in time, not wait until all was ready; when memory returned, continue the report.

literal: Morning and evening they were given imperial food; until sunset they listened afar.
idiomatic: Morning and evening they were given imperial food; until sunset they listened afar.

literal: At the time the hundred officials asked to establish the eastern palace; the edict did not grant it.
idiomatic: At the time the hundred officials asked to establish the eastern palace; the edict did not grant it.

literal: Each time Xi was sent to the eastern hall to oversee the crown prince's cap and robe, guiding and leading his pace in bowing.
idiomatic: Each time Wang Xi was sent to the eastern hall to oversee the crown prince's cap and robe, guiding and leading his pace in bowing.

literal: He was made grand tutor of the crown prince; Xi as office-holder received the seal and sash.
idiomatic: He was made grand tutor of the crown prince; Wang Xi as office-holder received the seal and sash.

literal: When the crown prince performed the capping sacrifice, he was also concurrently palace attendant.
idiomatic: When the crown prince performed the capping sacrifice, he was also concurrently palace attendant.

literal: The emperor said: "Now that you hold urgent office, you cannot as usual be leisurely and slow.
idiomatic: The emperor said, "Now that you hold urgent office, you cannot as usual be leisurely and slow.

literal: The emperor was about to campaign north; he ordered inquiry what was heard outside lately.
idiomatic: The emperor was about to campaign north; he ordered inquiry what was heard outside lately.

literal: Xi said: "On the roads they say the imperial carriage will march.
idiomatic: Wang Xi said, "On the roads they say the imperial carriage will march.

literal: " The emperor said: "The Kumo Xi raid south; I have not myself led arms — therefore I wish for the moment to drill soldiers.
idiomatic: " The emperor said, "The Kumo Xi raid south; I have not myself led arms — therefore I wish for the moment to drill soldiers.

literal: " Xi said: "Imperial tours for inspection may still pass; if lightly there is dispatch, I fear the realm will lose hope.
idiomatic: " Wang Xi said, "Imperial tours for inspection may still pass; if lightly there is dispatch, I fear the realm will lose hope.

literal: " The emperor said: "This is the coward's constant worry; I myself will weigh it when the time comes.
idiomatic: " The emperor said, "This is the coward's constant worry; I myself will weigh it when the time comes.

literal: The emperor had the Qi commander Pei Ze and document clerk Cai Hui spy on the host below, fond of mutual slander; court gentlemen called them Pei and Cai.
idiomatic: The emperor had the Qi commander Pei Ze and document clerk Cai Hui spy on the host below, fond of mutual slander; court gentlemen called them Pei and Cai.

literal: At that time the two reported that after the imperial carriage's northern campaign, people said Yang Xiuzhi and Wang Xi often feasted and wandered with others, not keeping public business in mind.
idiomatic: At that time the two reported that after the imperial carriage's northern campaign, people said Yang Xiuzhi and Wang Xi often feasted and wandered with others, not keeping public business in mind.

literal: The emperor flogged Xiuzhi and Xi each forty blows on the shins.
idiomatic: The emperor flogged Xiuzhi and Wang Xi each forty blows on the shins.

literal: The emperor beheaded a man before him and asked Xi: "Does this man deserve death?
idiomatic: The emperor beheaded a man before him and asked Wang Xi, "Does this man deserve death?

literal: " Xi said: "His crime indeed deserves death — only I regret he did not die in the proper place.
idiomatic: " Wang Xi said, "His crime indeed deserves death — only I regret he did not die in the proper place.

literal: I hear that punishing men in the market means abandoning them with the crowd; the palace hall is not a place for killing.
idiomatic: I hear that punishing men in the market means abandoning them with the crowd; the palace hall is not a place for killing.

literal: " The emperor changed countenance and said: "From now I shall change it for the princes.
idiomatic: " The emperor changed countenance and said, "From now I shall change it for the princes.

literal: The emperor wished to make Xi palace attendant; he firmly declined and would not accept.
idiomatic: The emperor wished to make Wang Xi palace attendant; he firmly declined and would not accept.

literal: Some urged Xi not to distance himself; Xi said: "From youth I have seen many men in power; puffed up for a little while, few did not end in ruin.
idiomatic: Some urged Wang Xi not to distance himself; Wang Xi said, "From youth I have seen many men in power; puffed up for a little while, few did not end in ruin.

literal: Moreover my nature is truly loose and slow, unfit for the times; a sovereign's private favor — how can it be kept? If by chance I lose restraint, there is nowhere to seek withdrawal.
idiomatic: Moreover my nature is truly loose and slow, unfit for the times; a sovereign's private favor — how can it be kept? If by chance I lose restraint, there is nowhere to seek withdrawal.

literal: It is not that I do not love the hot office — I have only chewed it over to the end.
idiomatic: It is not that I do not love the hot office — I have only chewed it over to the end.

literal: Once the hundred officials were granted an archery contest; Xi hit the target and should have received silk, but because he did not mark his arrow, the office would not give it.
idiomatic: Once the hundred officials were granted an archery contest; Wang Xi hit the target and should have received silk, but because he did not mark his arrow, the office would not give it.

literal: Xi said with easy content: "Today I may be called abundant in martial, short in literary.
idiomatic: Wang Xi said with easy content, "Today I may be called abundant in martial, short in literary.

literal: Xi had no son; the emperor would grant him a concubine; a yellow gate attendant went to his house to announce the edict; the empress also sent word to Xi's wife.
idiomatic: Wang Xi had no son; the emperor would grant him a concubine; a yellow gate attendant went to his house to announce the edict; the empress also sent word to Wang Xi's wife.

literal: Xi had his wife answer; the wife never spoke; Xi pat his chest with his hand and withdrew.
idiomatic: Wang Xi had his wife answer; the wife never spoke; Wang Xi patted his chest with his hand and withdrew.

literal: When the emperor heard it he laughed.
idiomatic: When the emperor heard it he laughed.

literal: When Emperor Xiaozhao died, he mourned almost beyond bearing and fell ill from weakness.
idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaozhao died, he mourned almost beyond bearing and fell ill from weakness.

literal: Emperor Wucheng had long resented his scholarly slowness and therefore disliked him the more; on presenting business he was roundly scolded, yet walked with elegant pace, unruffled.
idiomatic: Emperor Wucheng had long resented his scholarly slowness and therefore disliked him the more; on presenting business he was roundly scolded, yet walked with elegant pace, unruffled.

literal: He passed through posts as governor of eastern Xuzhou and director of the secretariat.
idiomatic: He passed through posts as governor of eastern Xuzhou and director of the secretariat.

literal: At the beginning of Wuping he was moved to grand director of ceremonies, given the same ceremonial rank as the three masters, supervised revision of the veritable records, and attended at the Forest of Literary Brilliance.
idiomatic: At the beginning of Wuping he was moved to grand director of ceremonies, given the same ceremonial rank as the three masters, supervised revision of the veritable records, and attended at the Forest of Literary Brilliance.

literal: His nature was leisurely and light in desire; though kingly affairs pressed thick, his refined conduct did not shift.
idiomatic: His nature was leisurely and light in desire; though kingly affairs pressed thick, his refined conduct did not shift.

literal: In Bing Province, though war horses filled the lanes, he never took worldly business as a burden.
idiomatic: In Bing Province, though war horses filled the lanes, he never took worldly business as a burden.

literal: On fine days and fair scenes he would chant and roam, climb hills and waters, making conversation and feasts his affair; gentlemen called him the marshal beyond things.
idiomatic: On fine days and fair scenes he would chant and roam, climb hills and waters, making conversation and feasts his affair; gentlemen called him the marshal beyond things.

literal: He often visited the Jin shrine and composed a poem: "The sun sets — I ought to go home; fish and birds seem to linger.
idiomatic: He often visited the Jin shrine and composed a poem: "The sun sets — I ought to go home; fish and birds seem to linger.

literal: Suddenly a messenger of the great prince arrived; he summoned Xi, who did not come at once.
idiomatic: Suddenly a messenger of the great prince arrived; he summoned Wang Xi, who did not come at once.
